# gs-secrets

> Poor-man's secret vault: a single-file CLI to store and retrieve API keys,
> passwords, and other secrets in an AES-256-GCM encrypted local vault.

## Documentation

- [README.md](README.md) — overview, installation, usage, and examples
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — threat model, file permissions, encryption details
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — development workflow and PR process
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) — version history (Keep a Changelog)
- [LICENSE](LICENSE) — MIT

## Quick start

```bash
go install github.com/guionardo/gs-secrets/cmd/gs-secrets@latest

gs-secrets --set github_token=ghp_xxxxxxxx --ttl 24h
gs-secrets --get github_token
gs-secrets --list
gs-secrets --delete github_token
```

## Installation

- Windows: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guionardo/gs-secrets/main/install.ps1 | iex`
- Other: download the release archive for your platform and verify against `checksums.txt`

## Commands

- `gs-secrets --set key=value [--ttl DURATION]` — store a secret (optional expiry)
- `gs-secrets --get key [--output FILE]` — print a secret
- `gs-secrets --delete key` — remove a secret
- `gs-secrets --list` — list keys
- `gs-secrets --version` — print version

Common flags: `--store PATH` (vault file), `--keyfile PATH` (master key
file), `--verbose` (diagnostics to stderr).

## Project layout

- `cmd/gs-secrets/` — thin entry point
- `internal/app/` — CLI logic: flag parsing, command dispatch
- `pkg/store/` — encrypted vault: AES-256-GCM, key-file management

## Security model (summary)

- AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption; random 32-byte key in
  `.gs-secrets.key` (0600) beside the vault (0600), directory 0700.
- Confidentiality rests on OS file permissions; backing up the key file is
  required for recovery. See SECURITY.md.

## Build & test

```bash
make build     # bin/gs-secrets
make test      # go test -race -cover ./...
make lint      # golangci-lint run ./...
make vulncheck # govulncheck
```

## Release process

Push a `v*` tag (e.g. `v1.2.3`); `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds
binaries for linux/darwin/windows (amd64+arm64), verifies the version,
generates checksums and a changelog, and publishes the GitHub release.
